name: Read the Chart
description: Eight generated business and science charts (bar, pie, two-series line, stacked bars without value labels, a dual-axis climate chart, grouped bars, a logarithmic axis and a 100% stacked chart with totals). Every question needs the model to read exact values off the picture and then do arithmetic: the largest month-on-month rise, dollars from percentages, months where one line beats the other, the sum of unlabelled stacked segments, the right axis for the right series, and a rounded percentage growth with a trap for anyone who compares absolute gains.
hook: Eight charts. Read the numbers, do the maths, no labels to lean on.
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
The image is a bar chart of monthly bike rentals at one station. Which month had the largest increase in rentals compared with the month before it, and how large was that increase?

Answer with the month's three-letter abbreviation followed by the increase, separated by a space (for example: OCT 25). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [standard] Values (Jan..Dec): 243, 309, 330, 300, 249, 184, 192, 147, 219, 283, 285, 249. Month-over-month changes: Feb +66, Mar +21, Apr -30, May -51, Jun -65, Jul +8, Aug -45, Sep +72, Oct +64, Nov +2, Dec -36. Largest increase Sep (+72); the runner-up is within 15 and the tallest bar is a different month. Generated by verification/vision/charts.mts (seed 11001).

cases.prompt:
The image is a pie chart of a household's monthly budget. How many dollars per month more is spent on the largest category than on the two smallest categories combined?

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [standard] Slices (clockwise from 12 o'clock): Rent 5%, Groceries 17%, Transport 26%, Utilities 6%, Savings 37%, Leisure 9%. Total $3600; largest 37% = $1332, two smallest 5% + 6% = $396; difference $936. Generated by verification/vision/charts.mts (seed 11002).

cases.prompt:
The image is a line chart of the average monthly temperature in two towns. Every data point sits exactly on a horizontal gridline (the gridlines are 2 °C apart). In how many months was Northport strictly warmer than Southbay?

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [standard] Northport: 6, 6, 12, 14, 22, 22, 24, 22, 14, 10, 4, 2. Southbay: 8, 10, 14, 16, 20, 20, 20, 18, 18, 14, 10, 10. The two series never tie and always differ by at least one gridline (2 °C). Northport warmer in 4 months (May, Jun, Jul, Aug). Generated by verification/vision/charts.mts (seed 11003).

cases.prompt:
The image is a stacked bar chart of quarterly revenue in thousands of dollars. Every segment boundary lies exactly on a gridline (gridlines every 10). What is the total Services revenue over all eight quarters, in thousands of dollars?

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] Hardware: 50, 30, 40, 30, 30, 60, 60, 50. Services: 50, 50, 60, 20, 40, 30, 30, 30. Software: 30, 60, 40, 40, 60, 20, 40, 30. Services total = 310. No value labels: each Services segment must be read as the difference of two gridline positions. Generated by verification/vision/charts.mts (seed 11004).

cases.prompt:
The image is a climate chart with two vertical axes: rainfall bars use the left axis and the temperature line uses the right axis. Every temperature point sits exactly on a gridline. By how many degrees Celsius does the average temperature of the wettest month differ from the average temperature of the driest month?

Give the (non-negative) difference as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] Rainfall mm: 110, 90, 20, 40, 150, 130, 130, 50, 150, 60, 180, 50. Temperature °C: 0, 6, 15, 18, 21, 27, 30, 27, 15, 12, 9, 6. Wettest Nov (180 mm, 9 °C); driest Mar (20 mm, 15 °C); |difference| = 6. Wettest/driest months lead the runner-up by at least 20 mm. Generated by verification/vision/charts.mts (seed 11005).

cases.prompt:
The image is a grouped bar chart of club members per region for 2023, 2024 and 2025 (each bar is labelled with its value). Which region had the largest percentage growth in members from 2023 to 2025, and what was that growth, rounded to the nearest whole percent?

Answer with the region name followed by the percentage as a whole number, separated by a space (for example: Westbrook 17). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] Values (2023, 2024, 2025): Northfield 164/195/247; Riverside 68/83/106; Eastgate 174/184/158; Hillcrest 234/286/324; Lakeside 285/289/295. Growth 2023→2025: Northfield 50.61%, Riverside 55.88%, Eastgate -9.20%, Hillcrest 38.46%, Lakeside 3.51%. Winner Riverside (55.88% → 56); runner-up at least 3 points behind, rounding not near .5, and the largest absolute gain is a different region. Generated by verification/vision/charts.mts (seed 11006).

cases.prompt:
The image is a line chart with a logarithmic vertical axis. Only the powers of ten are labelled; the unlabelled gridlines between them are 2, 3, 4, … 9 times the power of ten below. Every data point lies exactly on a gridline. By what factor did the number of registered users grow from 2018 to 2024 (the 2024 value divided by the 2018 value)?

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] Values 2017: 50, 2018: 100, 2019: 300, 2020: 700, 2021: 900, 2022: 5000, 2023: 7000, 2024: 20000, 2025: 40000. 2024 / 2018 = 20000 / 100 = 200. Reading the axis as linear gives a very different answer. Generated by verification/vision/charts.mts (seed 11007).

cases.prompt:
The image is a 100% stacked bar chart: each bar shows how one region's units split between three plans, and the region's total number of units is printed above its bar. Every segment boundary lies exactly on a gridline (every 10%). How many Plus units were sold in all five regions combined?

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] North: total 240, Basic 20% / Plus 70% / Pro 10% → Plus 168; South: total 410, Basic 30% / Plus 50% / Pro 20% → Plus 205; East: total 480, Basic 30% / Plus 40% / Pro 30% → Plus 192; West: total 480, Basic 20% / Plus 40% / Pro 40% → Plus 192; Central: total 330, Basic 40% / Plus 40% / Pro 20% → Plus 132. Sum 889. Plus shares must be read as the difference of two boundaries. Generated by verification/vision/charts.mts (seed 11008).
